title: In Vitro, Ex Vivo and In Vivo Characterization of Cytocompatibility and Biocompatibility of a Cross-linked Fish Collagen Wound Membrane
authors: Jung, O., Burckhardt, K., Stammkoetter, S., Barrientos, M. M., Reinholdt, C., Andreeva, T., Stošić, M. R., Stojanović, S., Najman, S., Krastev, R., Walther, F., Pantermehl, S., & Barbeck, M. (2025). In vivo (Athens, Greece), 39(5), 2517–2533. 3
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss Jason membrane (porcine pericardium) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “The results of this study highlight the potential of fish collagen membranes as biocompatible wound healing materials. However, their rapid degradation presents a challenge that needs to be addressed through targeted modifications, such as optimized cross-linking” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
